output.summary: ED nurse staffing is flat and at grid, and visits, acuity and bed capacity are unchanged. About 3.0 of the 3.2 hour rise sits in boarding. Boarding jumped in March and April, when the hospitalist rounding change delayed medical-ward discharges. Surgical wards, which were not changed, show no shift. The 4 West huddle pilot used a schedule fixed beforehand, and it cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours. So extend the huddle and track it weekly. A discharge lounge is a reasonable extra. Restoring evening cleaning is premature, since there is no turnaround data. The travel-nurse contract defers case managers, and pausing the huddle removes the proven control. Both would worsen boarding. Door-to-provider and left-without-being-seen are confounded by the May triage-provider cut.
